question: A smaller circle touches a bigger circle internally and also passes through the center 'O' of the bigger circle. If the area of the smaller circle is 192 cm², the area of the bigger circle (in cm²) is:
solution:
Given:

A smaller circle touches a bigger circle internally and also passes through the center 'O' of the bigger circle.

The area of the smaller circle is 192 cm2.

Concept used:

1. Area of a circle = πR2 (R = Radius)

2. Radius × 2 = Diameter

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b5ca0c47d38a6487116fe64dc5725db3776b8f3683445764980f06dcfeea287.png] 

According to the figure,

Since the smaller circle touches a bigger circle internally and also passes through the center 'O' of the bigger circle, CD is the diameter of the smaller circle while CD is the radius of the bigger circle.

Let the radius of the smaller circle be R.

So, the radius of the bigger circle = 2R

Area of the bigger circle = π × (2R)2

According to the concept,

πR² = 192

⇒ 4 × πR2 = 4 × 192

⇒ π × (2R)² = 768

**∴ The area of the bigger circle will be 768 cm².**
